title: TSMGen: Target-Specific Molecule Generation via Higher-Order Structural Dependencies and Context-Aware Bidirectional Fusion
claim: Our model encodes pocket and molecule inputs through dedicated modules, then fuses them bidirectionally to generate target-specific outputs.
layout: 4 panels (a–d); left-to-right flow, bottom row inputs, zoomed fusion panel at right
description: A four-panel framework diagram. Panel (a), top left on a gray background, shows a protein pocket split into two branches. The upper branch is a hypergraph with a hypergraph neural network, drawn as node extraction, hyperedge representations and node feature updates. The lower branch is an atomic graph with message passing, with equations and a Jumping Knowledge Network. Each branch ends in linear scoring, softmax and Set2Set pooling blocks, giving 1×256 vectors that are combined by a circled plus into F_fusion. Panel (b), bottom left, takes a SMILES string through an embedding layer and position encoding into a green feature grid. Panel (c) holds self-attention, a BGCA block and a feedforward layer, repeated ×8, and outputs a 3D generated molecule. Panel (d), at right, shows gated cross-attention. Molecule and pocket features query each other through crossing arrows, and the two results are added element-wise into F_Com. The panels use soft blue, purple, green and yellow tints.
caption: Framework of the proposed TSMGen. (a) Residue-level hypergraph and Atomic-level structure representation of protein pockets. (b) Feature representation of molecules. (c) Molecule generation module. (d) Context-aware bidirectional fusion.
abstract: Efficiently designing high-quality molecules targeting disease-relevant targets is a critical challenge. Most existing methods can capture pairwise amino acid relations, neglecting the higher-order relations among multiple amino acids. This paper proposes a target-specific molecule generation framework, namely TSMGen, to comprehensively capture the local and global structural information of the protein pocket by modeling higher-order spatial dependencies both at the atomic and the amino acid levels. Furthermore, we design a context-aware bidirectional fusion module to learn the more detailed structural information about the protein pocket. This module simultaneously attends to features from both the protein pocket and the molecule, fully leveraging the structural information from both to optimize the generation process of targeted molecules, thereby enhancing the quality of generated molecules. Experiments show that TSMGen outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of Vina Score, High Affinity, QED, SA and Diversity, and a case study on $\beta$-secretase enzyme further confirms its ability to generate molecules with stronger binding affinity.
